note: Current readings for the other-signals panel; the backtest's history comes from pipeline/backtest/data/econ (FRED) and retirements.csv. Each item: what it is, the latest value, the comparison, the source page that states it.

items.label: Consumer sentiment (University of Michigan)
items.say: Near the lowest readings in the survey's history; sentiment has been low under both parties since 2022.

items.label: Gasoline, national average (AAA)
items.compare: $3.066 a year ago; $4.334 a week ago; $4.475 a month ago
items.say: Up about 39% in a year, though about 6 cents lower than a week ago and 20 cents below a month ago.

items.label: A Chipotle chicken burrito bowl
items.say: Roughly 15–20% more than four years ago; restaurant prices overall are up 3.4% in the past year (CPI food away from home, August).
items.src: Reuters via ThePricer (May 2026); Food Business News (Oct 2022)

items.label: Prediction markets: Democratic House
items.compare: Senate: about 68% Democratic from the balance-of-power contracts (Democrats win both 68¢ on Kalshi and 67.5¢ on Polymarket; Democratic House with Republican Senate 22.5¢ and 24.5¢; Republican House with Democratic Senate under 1¢; Republicans win both 8.6¢ and 7.5¢)
items.say: Markets sit between the polls-only model and the expert raters.

items.label: Cook Political Report House ratings
items.compare: Cook's likely range (Oct 9): Democrats gain 9-19 seats, 224-234; after 11 more moves toward Democrats on Oct 16: Solid/Likely/Lean D 214, Toss Up 21, Lean/Likely/Solid R 200. Senate (Oct 20): 7 Toss Ups, 6 Republican-held, after South Carolina and Mississippi moved toward Democrats and Minnesota toward Republicans
items.say: Democrats need a fifth of the toss-ups for a majority if the seats leaning their way hold.

items.label: House members not seeking re-election
items.say: More Republicans leaving, including 20 running for other office; retirements have not tracked the swing in past midterms.
